posts.text: "This Supreme Court decision may still end up being a political victory for Republicans, but it isn’t as straightforward as it looks." Bill Galston, Elaine Kamarck, and Jordan Muchnick analyze this week's SCOTUS decision on redistricting and its ultimate electoral impacts. brook.gs/49ag0J9

For Second Chance Month, Keesha Middlemass examines how clean slate laws—passed in 13 states and D.C.—are reducing barriers to employment, housing, and economic opportunity for the 1 in 3 U.S. adults with a criminal record. brook.gs/4cYE5ns

The law governing how companies like Google, Meta, and Verizon hand over your data to law enforcement was written in 1986—before smartphones, cloud storage, or chatbots existed. Stephanie K. Pell and Richard Salgado make the case for updating it. brook.gs/4ugSYs8

A new oil shock is driving up the price of gas for Americans, putting disproportionate pressure on lower-income households and residents of car-dependent communities. Adie Tomer and Ben Swedberg examine how gas prices impact regions differently and what it could mean for long-term transportation and energy policy reforms. brook.gs/4cR67Bk

The wave of recent redistricting battles may be nearing its end, but the consequences could reshape congressional maps for years. Elaine Kamarck breaks down where things stand, from Virginia to Florida. brook.gs/4ecRHxM

What did "Life, Liberty, and the pursuit of Happiness" really mean in 1776, and how has its meaning evolved since? Katie Dunn Tenpas talks with Lindsay Chervinsky, recorded at the George Washington Presidential Library at Mount Vernon. brook.gs/4eOxMFk

All 56 of the nation's major metro areas saw immigration decline—and nearly all of them felt it in their population numbers. William Frey breaks down what the data mean for cities' demographic and economic futures. brook.gs/4ub5p95
And his companion piece examines the race- and place-based factors shaping who bears the burden as homeowners insurance markets grow less stable: brook.gs/4mL4Cco
New research from Manann maps where rising climate risks and insurance costs will hit hardest—and which communities are least equipped to absorb them: brook.gs/4vK0VI3

The climate conversation has long centered on emissions reductions. Manann Donoghoe explains why affordability, not just emissions, should be at the center of the climate conversation.

Video

The core flaw of the JCPOA wasn't the details, it was the expiration dates. Michael O'Hanlon makes the case for a permanent Iran nuclear agreement, and explains where the U.S. can afford to be flexible. brook.gs/4mLGlD8

"The Iranians believe that time is on their side."
 
Suzanne Maloney on @NPRWeekend Sunday, assessing where U.S.-Iran nuclear negotiations stand—and why a durable agreement remains elusive. brook.gs/4cTPPIR

Small and midsized city downtowns hold real promise—but vacant parcels, idle public land, and excess parking are holding many back.

Tracy Hadden Loh, Hanna Love, and Bethany Krupicka identify key challenges and offer four recommendations for downtown recovery that can apply to cities of all sizes. brook.gs/4vArtLy

The Fed's regional banks run on a $5.9B budget and employ 85% of the Federal Reserve's workforce—yet much of the underlying infrastructure hasn't kept pace with the 21st century. Fed Governor Christopher Waller joins us April 21 to talk modernization. 

Attend in person or watch online 👇 brook.gs/3Qu8ORz

What does China's new Five-Year Plan tell us about where its economy is headed? On the latest episode of The Beijing Brief, @jonczin, @andrewpolk81, and @kyleichan break down Beijing's big bet on technology and innovation—and what the plan's ambitions mean for global trade, manufacturing, and competition.

Listen to the episode 👇 brook.gs/4cKA4UG
